name: Amoebic Liver Abscess

possible: Concurrent or preceding intestinal amoebiasis (only a minority have concurrent diarrhea at presentation)
pathogens.why: Entamoeba histolytica is the specific cause of amoebic liver abscess, reaching the liver via the portal circulation after invading the colonic mucosa; the classic presentation is a single right-lobe abscess, which helps but does not definitively distinguish it from pyogenic abscess without aspirate/serology.

investigations.why: Characterizes the abscess (typically single, right lobe, in amoebic disease) and guides the decision on aspiration.
Highly sensitive for invasive amoebiasis and useful when aspiration is not performed or is inconclusive.
Supportive if positive, but a substantial proportion of liver abscess patients have negative stool studies at the time of presentation.

investigations.test: Diagnostic aspiration (if no improvement in 5-7 days, large/left-lobe abscess, or diagnostic uncertainty)
investigations.why: Classic 'anchovy paste' aspirate supports amoebic etiology; also allows bacterial culture to exclude/identify a pyogenic or mixed process.

reasonSource: ()=>"Right upper quadrant pain and fever without jaundice, in a patient from an endemic area (with or without a preceding diarrheal illness), raises suspicion for amoebic liver abscess — a classically single, right-lobe lesion caused by Entamoeba histolytica. This is distinguished from pyogenic liver abscess primarily by aspirate appearance/serology, but empiric metronidazole is appropriate to start given the high treatment success rate and relative safety, pending confirmation."
